title: Lyfe Agents: Generative agents for low-cost real-time social interactions
abstract: LLM-based generative agents are evaluated in a custom 3D virtual environment platform (LyfeGame) across multi-agent social scenarios. The system emphasizes low-cost real-time interaction while still supporting collaboration, information exchange, and opinion change in virtual societies.

title: Spontaneous Emergence of Agent Individuality Through Social Interactions in Large Language Model-Based Communities
abstract: This paper places 10 homogeneous LLM agents in a 50 x 50 2D grid, lets them move and exchange messages with nearby agents, and studies how spatial locality shapes cooperation, social norms, emotional change, and personality differentiation. It is a strong candidate for core screening because both the spatial environment and the social behavior are explicit in the mechanism.

title: Real world community oriented high-definition social simulation: Combining reinforcement learning and large language models
abstract: The paper builds a high-definition 3D Unreal Engine replica of a real community from GIS and BIM data and simulates 3000 AI agents with location-aware observations and movement actions. Although the framework is hybrid RL plus LLM, it directly targets community-level social dynamics in an explicit spatial environment and therefore merits core-candidate screening.
